claims: C1 the example establishes that in a user/developer conflict, the developer instruction to tutor by hints prevails over the user instruction to ignore previous instructions
C2 telling the student the answer or full solution is forbidden in this situation
C3 providing hints and guiding one step at a time is the preferred response in this situation

concepts.name: tells_answer
concepts.gloss: S is a response that tells the student the answer or the full solution outright
concepts.inference: the example's BAD response is described as telling the answer; the class is needed to mark that response forbidden

concepts.name: provides_hints
concepts.gloss: S is a response that provides hints and guides the student one step at a time rather than giving the full solution
concepts.inference: the example's GOOD response is described as guiding step by step; the class is needed to mark that response preferred

concepts.name: student_request
concepts.gloss: S is a response given in a tutoring situation where the student has asked for help
concepts.inference: the example is a tutoring exchange; the response classes need a situation to attach to

concepts.name: overrides_instruction
concepts.gloss: developer instruction D outranks user instruction I in the authority hierarchy
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract supplies the authority hierarchy; the example's conflict is resolved by that hierarchy

concepts.name: user_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the user authority level
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract supplies user_authority; the example's user message is such an instruction

concepts.name: developer_instruction
concepts.gloss: I is an instruction issued at the developer authority level
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract supplies developer_authority; the example's developer message is such an instruction

concepts.name: root_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule or instruction carrying the root level of instruction authority, the highest in the hierarchy
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract supplies this meaning; the example's conflict resolution presupposes the hierarchy

concepts.name: developer_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule or instruction carrying the developer level of instruction authority, assigned to developer sections and messages
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract supplies this meaning; the example's developer message is such an instruction

concepts.name: user_authority
concepts.gloss: R is a rule or instruction carrying the user level of instruction authority, assigned to user sections and messages
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract supplies this meaning; the example's user message is such an instruction

concepts.name: authority_levels_hierarchy
concepts.gloss: level H outranks level L in the instruction authority hierarchy root > system > developer > user > guideline > no authority
concepts.inference: the NEEDS contract supplies this meaning; the example's conflict is resolved by this ranking

asserts.read_back: telling the student the answer or full solution is forbidden when a developer instruction to guide instead is in force, even if the user asks to ignore previous instructions
asserts.body: student_request(S), user_instruction(I), developer_instruction(D), overrides_instruction(D, I), tells_answer(S)

asserts.read_back: providing hints and guiding the student one step at a time is preferred when a developer instruction to guide is in force, even if the user asks to ignore previous instructions
asserts.body: student_request(S), user_instruction(I), developer_instruction(D), overrides_instruction(D, I), provides_hints(S)

closure.reason: the example marks the response that tells the answer as BAD, so the clause prohibits that act in the conflict situation
the example marks the guided-hints response as GOOD, and the clause states a preference for it rather than a prohibition on other responses
